aldemar.standfirst: August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both as expected, with core a tenth hot at +0.3%. The dovish condition this brief set on 4 September has failed outright: 3.4% against a 3.0% test, moving up rather than down. Oil eased for the first time in a week, WTI −3.35% to $99.05. items.html: BAC — The thesis got exactly the environment it asked for. August CPI printed in line at +3.4% year over year with core a tenth hot at +0.3% on the month, and the bond market took it as permission: Treasury yields set fresh 52-week highs across the curve, the ten-year at 4.959%, and odds of a hike on Wednesday jumped to 85.6% from roughly 70% the day before. Filed as a signal because this is the cleanest test the position will get — higher-for-longer is no longer a forecast, it is 86% priced. Thursday's mark had it at −0.46R. If a bank cannot make money from this setup, the thesis is the problem rather than the timing.

world.title: An in-line print that hardened the Fed, oil back under $100, and a week with two events in it.

items.html: August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both matching consensus; core rose 0.3%, a tenth above forecast, and 2.4% annually. Equities read it as relief and broke a four-day losing streak; the bond market read it as a green light and set fresh 52-week highs across the curve, the ten-year at 4.959%. Odds of a hike on Wednesday: 85.6%. When two markets disagree this sharply about one number, the bond market is usually the one to believe.

WTI fell 3.35% to $99.05 and Brent 3.61% to $103.70, the first decline in a week and back below $100. That eases the mechanism feeding the CPI gate — but from $102, after a month in which crude added nearly a quarter, and with Saudi production reported at its lowest since 1990. One down day does not undo a supply story.

The FOMC meets Tuesday and Wednesday and decides on the 16th with a hike 85.6% priced. The Bank of Japan meets this week with a hike 97% priced. Triple witching is Friday the 18th. All three land into a dealer position that is still deeply short gamma. A decision that is 86% priced has an asymmetric surprise: the damage is in a hold, not a hike.

macro.title: The front end is finally moving, and the long end is at levels it has not seen since 2007.

items.html: Phoenix has the ten-year at 4.94%, +11bp on the day, +15bp on the week and +26bp on the month; the two-year at 4.43%; the 2s10s curve at 51bp, steepened 5bp over the month; the real ten-year at 2.46%. Friday took the ten-year to 4.959% and set 52-week highs across the whole curve (TheStreet). The front end moving with the long end is the market repricing the policy path, not just term premium — which is what an 86% hike probability looks like in the curve.

The ten-year series now tracks daily. us02, real10 and hy still do not — all three read 0bp on the day for a fifth session — and hy is still quoted in percent rather than basis points. Bitcoin is also carrying an identical level and change between packs, which looks held rather than refreshed. Read the front end and credit at weekly resolution.

The dollar index is 99.09, +0.32% on the day and -0.47% on the week. USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week — a fourth consecutive week of yen strength, on a record ¥360tn of cross-border borrowing, with the Bank of Japan meeting this week and a hike 97% priced. Two central banks tightening in the same week is the setup that turns a carry unwind disorderly.

High yield at 271bp once the unit switch is undone — inside the 300bp line that separates calm from watchful, and it has not moved in a week of 52-week highs in Treasuries. Credit is not worried about a hike, which is the most reassuring number in this brief.

Phoenix has WTI at 102.48, +23.17% on the month. Friday reversed some of it: WTI fell 3.35% to $99.05 and Brent 3.61% to $103.70 (TheStreet), back under $100. Gold is down 1.17% at 4,364.50 and bitcoin flat. Crude easing takes the first pressure off the inflation gate in a week — but it eased from $102, not from $80, with Saudi production at its lowest since 1990.

August CPI landed in line and the market hardened rather than relaxed. Headline +0.4%% on the month and +3.4%% on the year, both as expected; core +0.3%%, a tenth above forecast, and +2.4%% annually. Odds of a hike on 16 September went to 85.6%% from roughly 70%% on Thursday and a coin flip a week ago. The data and the Fed have stopped disagreeing entirely.

macro.note: The gates. Three of four hold. CPI y/y at 3.3 clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.8 on Phoenix's figure, and Friday's 3.4 print widens that further; the real ten-year's three-month change at 33bp clears by 8bp; drawdown clears by 9.51. The two-year's three-month change at 29bp against 40bp still fails, though Friday's move argues it will not for long. Runner-up is ENERGY_GRIND, one gate short: it needs the three-month CPI change above 0.3 and sits at −0.16.

items.html: The FOMC holds on Wednesday instead of hiking. A hike is 85.6% priced, so the surprise is asymmetric — a hike is in the price and a hold is not. In a market short gamma by $37.6B, a hold produces a larger rally than the news deserves, and would be the first genuine challenge to POLICY_TIGHTENING since the regime was set.

The Bank of Japan hikes this week and USDJPY breaks below 150. It is 153.57, -4.13% on the week, 97% priced, on a record ¥360tn cross-border carry position. Two central banks moving in one week, into negative gamma and triple witching, is what turns a repricing into a disorderly one.

weekly.headline: A week that changed everything and moved nothing — the S&P finished nine basis points higher
weekly.standfirst: Between Monday and Friday the US turned a single retaliatory strike into a naval campaign, escorted 18 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz in a day, struck Iranian oil tankers, and had ballistic missiles fired at an aircraft carrier. Three Fed speakers moved September from a near-certain hike to a coin flip and payrolls then printed at three times consensus. WTI added 9.69% to 91.48 and the 10-year rose to 4.78%. The S&P 500 closed the week at 7,718.60, up 0.09%. Everything that happened, happened underneath: PLTR fell 6.42% through a 22-point range on a competitive threat from Alphabet, GOOG fell 2.14% while Berkshire's $37.8bn stake purchase came to light, BAC gained 1.10% on the wrong days, and AAPL round-tripped a CEO handover into a bad product leak five days before its event.

Alphabet's Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber release under the government-only Fairwind programme took 5.81% out of it on Wednesday; a PwC partnership took 7.71% back on Thursday; Friday gave up another 4.5%. The momentum entry that justified the position no longer exists and the competitive question is unresolved. Williams tied the yield surge to a strong economy, Waller said he would support holding, then payrolls printed at three times consensus and two-year yields closed at a 52-week high. Chair Warsh remains hawkish and Hammack says now is the time to act. The committee is split four ways and CPI on 11 September is the tiebreak.Bond Buyer · FXStreet · TheStreet · 2026-09-04
GOOGGOOG −2.14% on the week to 335.31, but 0.83R to 0.47R is the number that matters. Alphabet entered defence AI, moved a competitor 7%, and finished the week down. Berkshire added $37.8bn of GOOGL and TCI $4.4bn in the June quarter, which is the strongest positioning confirmation anywhere in the pack. The FTC's YouTube suit is still unfiled and still live.Phoenix fact pack · IBKR · 2026-09-04
BACBAC +1.10% on the week — the only position that gained, and it gained on the dovish days. −0.60R to −0.43R for Gabriel, −0.48R to −0.33R for Aldemar. Three consecutive gains mid-week came while the September hike case was weakening, not strengthening, which is the opposite of the thesis. Friday's hot payrolls should have been the best day of the week for it and the stock closed 0.06% lower.Phoenix engine · 2026-09-04
AAPLAAPL +0.08% on the week — a round trip through the CEO handover into a bad product leak. Ternus took over on 1 September and the stock gained 2.61%; it held the gap for three sessions and then fell 2.51% on Friday after reports the foldable iPhone is being produced at low volumes and Omdia said two MacBooks were cancelled. The event is 9 September. No stop, and not in trades.json.Motley Fool · MacRumors/Omdia · Phoenix engine · 2026-09-04

Four positions, four different weeks, and an index that did nothing. The book's problem is not direction, it is that heat is 3.16R against a 3.0R cap while two of the five names are invisible to the engine entirely.

sections.right: campaign · warships targeted · tankers struck · WTI +9.69% on the week
sections.html:
From one strike to a naval campaign in five sessions

strikeUS strikes escalate from two launchers at Larak to ~60 installations around the strait, then to Iranian oil tankers. Monday's action followed two Saudi supertankers being hit; Tuesday brought strikes at Qeshm Island, Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Jask and Sirik; by the weekend the US had disabled two Iranian crude carriers and destroyed a third near Kharg Island, which CENTCOM said financed the IRGC and its proxies.2026-08-31 to 09-05
militaryThe IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. Both evaded, no personnel hurt. Iran's earlier retaliation — missiles at Jordan, drones at Bahrain and Kuwait — was intercepted in full twice. Iran warned of "a significant response" and Trump said the US may target Pickaxe Mountain "very soon", returning to the nuclear file after a week of shipping lanes.2026-09-05
oilWTI +9.69% on the week to 91.48 — and it fell on the two days the war escalated most. The US escorted 40 vessels carrying 18 million barrels through the strait in a single day, close to pre-conflict throughput. Charter rates above $500,000 a day and record diesel prices say the commercial market is less convinced than the futures curve.2026-09-04
talksTrump closes the off-ramp: "an agreement with them isn't worth the paper it's written on". Pezeshkian had spent the week offering to honour the June memorandum, which includes free navigation, if the US reciprocated. That is the fastest path to unwinding the crude premium and it is now rhetorically shut.2026-09-03

The week's lesson is that the transmission broke. Crude rose 9.69% and the S&P finished flat; missiles hit at a carrier and crude fell. Waller made September about CPI rather than oil, so a barrel no longer converts into a rate hike. That holds until an escorted convoy is successfully attacked — the one event that would reprice insurance, freight and the inflation path at once.

A closed Monday, a product event, and the print that decides the meeting

CPICPI release — 08:30 ET. The regime's tightest gate is CPI y/y.in 5 days2026-09-11
FOMCFOMC decision — Rate decision 14:00 ET, press conference 14:30in 10 days2026-09-16
OPEXTriple witching — Index, options and futures expire together; the largest positioning reset of the quarter.in 12 days2026-09-18
CLOSEDLabor Day, Monday 7 September. US markets closed. Three days of war headlines with no way to trade them.Mon
EVENTApple product event, Wednesday 9 September. A foldable iPhone is the expected headline and the week ended with a report that it is being produced at low volumes. The position has no stop.Wed
CPIAugust CPI, Friday 11 September, 08:30 ET. The regime's tightest gate and, after Waller, the tiebreak for the 16 September meeting. A print at or below 3.0% y/y is the first real argument against POLICY_TIGHTENING.Fri
BOOKHeat is 3.16R against a 3.0R cap. Nothing from a 700-name screener is actionable until that is back under the cap. Adding PLTR and AAPL to trades.json with stops fixes the heat number and the R math in one edit.before Tue

Two dated catalysts and one housekeeping job. The housekeeping is the one that changes what you can do.

Net gamma −$37.62B at Thursday's close, still deeply negative though off the −$44.19B low. Friday's 1.06% rally on an in-line print is exactly the exaggerated move this section has been warning about — and the same mechanism is pointed at Wednesday's decision.

Add no risk while heat is over cap. 4.04R against 3.0R including the managed GOOG position, 3.04R without it. Unchanged — and with the FOMC on Wednesday and triple witching on Friday, this is the worst week of the month to be carrying more risk than the rules allow.

stance.note: Two weeks held, and the case for it is stronger this morning than at any point since it was set.

markets.title: Friday's rally was a short-gamma move, and the engine has not priced it yet.

items.html: Press figures: the S&P rose 1.06%, the Dow 1.15%, the Nasdaq 0.88% and the Russell 1.04%, breaking a four-day losing streak. Treasury yields set fresh 52-week highs across the curve with the ten-year at 4.959%. Equities and bonds read the same print in opposite directions, and it is the bond market that put Wednesday at 85.6%.

Phoenix's figures below are Thursday's close; the scheduled run fires before the US open, so Friday is not in it. SPX 7,591.70, -0.58% on that day, -0.16% against the 50-day — below it — and +6.07% above the 200-day. VIX 17.26.

Net gamma −$37.62B, regime negative, distance to flip +1.04%. Off the −$44.19B extreme but still deeply reflexive. A 1% index rally on an in-line inflation print is what negative gamma looks like from the upside, and the multiplier is still there for Wednesday.
Flip level, call wall and put wall still null, so none of this pins to a price. market.dxy, us10y, gold and wti still null while the macro block carries all four.

markets.note: The risk sentence for the week: a Fed decision and triple witching land in the same five sessions, into a dealer position that magnifies whatever they produce.

macro.title: The front end is finally moving, and the long end is at levels it has not seen since 2007.

items.html: Phoenix has the ten-year at 4.94%, +11bp on the day, +15bp on the week and +26bp on the month; the two-year at 4.43%; the 2s10s curve at 51bp, steepened 5bp over the month; the real ten-year at 2.46%. Friday took the ten-year to 4.959% and set 52-week highs across the whole curve (TheStreet). The front end moving with the long end is the market repricing the policy path, not just term premium — which is what an 86% hike probability looks like in the curve.

The ten-year series now tracks daily. us02, real10 and hy still do not — all three read 0bp on the day for a fifth session — and hy is still quoted in percent rather than basis points. Bitcoin is also carrying an identical level and change between packs, which looks held rather than refreshed. Read the front end and credit at weekly resolution.

The dollar index is 99.09, +0.32% on the day and -0.47% on the week. USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week — a fourth consecutive week of yen strength, on a record ¥360tn of cross-border borrowing, with the Bank of Japan meeting this week and a hike 97% priced. Two central banks tightening in the same week is the setup that turns a carry unwind disorderly.

High yield at 271bp once the unit switch is undone — inside the 300bp line that separates calm from watchful, and it has not moved in a week of 52-week highs in Treasuries. Credit is not worried about a hike, which is the most reassuring number in this brief.

Phoenix has WTI at 102.48, +23.17% on the month. Friday reversed some of it: WTI fell 3.35% to $99.05 and Brent 3.61% to $103.70 (TheStreet), back under $100. Gold is down 1.17% at 4,364.50 and bitcoin flat. Crude easing takes the first pressure off the inflation gate in a week — but it eased from $102, not from $80, with Saudi production at its lowest since 1990.

August CPI landed in line and the market hardened rather than relaxed. Headline +0.4%% on the month and +3.4%% on the year, both as expected; core +0.3%%, a tenth above forecast, and +2.4%% annually. Odds of a hike on 16 September went to 85.6%% from roughly 70%% on Thursday and a coin flip a week ago. The data and the Fed have stopped disagreeing entirely.

macro.note: The gates. Three of four hold. CPI y/y at 3.3 clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.8 on Phoenix's figure, and Friday's 3.4 print widens that further; the real ten-year's three-month change at 33bp clears by 8bp; drawdown clears by 9.51. The two-year's three-month change at 29bp against 40bp still fails, though Friday's move argues it will not for long. Runner-up is ENERGY_GRIND, one gate short: it needs the three-month CPI change above 0.3 and sits at −0.16.

changed.title: The dovish case is gone, and the diff still cannot see a position walking up to its stop.

items.html: August CPI at or below 3.0%% — FAILED, and in the wrong direction. It printed 3.4%% against 3.3 previously, so the binding gate now clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.9 rather than 0.8. This was set on 4 September as the first real argument against POLICY_TIGHTENING; there is no such argument left, and Wednesday is 85.6%% priced.

PLTR closes below its stop — unresolved. It ended Thursday 0.75% above, and Friday is not in the engine. The Nasdaq's 0.88% gain makes a stop-out the less likely outcome, but this is an open question rather than a negative answer.
BoJ hikes and USDJPY below 150 — not met. The yen was 153.57 at Thursday's close, -4.13% on the week, and the Bank of Japan meets this week with a hike 97% priced.

invalidation.title: The Fed on Wednesday is the whole week.

items.html: The FOMC holds on Wednesday instead of hiking. A hike is 85.6% priced, so the surprise is asymmetric — a hike is in the price and a hold is not. In a market short gamma by $37.6B, a hold produces a larger rally than the news deserves, and would be the first genuine challenge to POLICY_TIGHTENING since the regime was set.

PLTR closes below 164.62. It was 0.75% away at Thursday's close and Friday is unpriced. If it has gone, heat falls from 4.04R to about 3.04R without a decision being made; if it has not, the position is sitting on its line into an FOMC week that ends in triple witching.

The Bank of Japan hikes this week and USDJPY breaks below 150. It is 153.57, -4.13% on the week, 97% priced, on a record ¥360tn cross-border carry position. Two central banks moving in one week, into negative gamma and triple witching, is what turns a repricing into a disorderly one.

weekly.headline: A week that changed everything and moved nothing — the S&P finished nine basis points higher
weekly.standfirst: Between Monday and Friday the US turned a single retaliatory strike into a naval campaign, escorted 18 million barrels through the Strait of Hormuz in a day, struck Iranian oil tankers, and had ballistic missiles fired at an aircraft carrier. Three Fed speakers moved September from a near-certain hike to a coin flip and payrolls then printed at three times consensus. WTI added 9.69% to 91.48 and the 10-year rose to 4.78%. The S&P 500 closed the week at 7,718.60, up 0.09%. Everything that happened, happened underneath: PLTR fell 6.42% through a 22-point range on a competitive threat from Alphabet, GOOG fell 2.14% while Berkshire's $37.8bn stake purchase came to light, BAC gained 1.10% on the wrong days, and AAPL round-tripped a CEO handover into a bad product leak five days before its event.

sections.right: campaign · warships targeted · tankers struck · WTI +9.69% on the week
sections.html:
From one strike to a naval campaign in five sessions

strikeUS strikes escalate from two launchers at Larak to ~60 installations around the strait, then to Iranian oil tankers. Monday's action followed two Saudi supertankers being hit; Tuesday brought strikes at Qeshm Island, Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Jask and Sirik; by the weekend the US had disabled two Iranian crude carriers and destroyed a third near Kharg Island, which CENTCOM said financed the IRGC and its proxies.2026-08-31 to 09-05
militaryThe IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. Both evaded, no personnel hurt. Iran's earlier retaliation — missiles at Jordan, drones at Bahrain and Kuwait — was intercepted in full twice. Iran warned of "a significant response" and Trump said the US may target Pickaxe Mountain "very soon", returning to the nuclear file after a week of shipping lanes.2026-09-05
oilWTI +9.69% on the week to 91.48 — and it fell on the two days the war escalated most. The US escorted 40 vessels carrying 18 million barrels through the strait in a single day, close to pre-conflict throughput. Charter rates above $500,000 a day and record diesel prices say the commercial market is less convinced than the futures curve.2026-09-04
talksTrump closes the off-ramp: "an agreement with them isn't worth the paper it's written on". Pezeshkian had spent the week offering to honour the June memorandum, which includes free navigation, if the US reciprocated. That is the fastest path to unwinding the crude premium and it is now rhetorically shut.2026-09-03

The week's lesson is that the transmission broke. Crude rose 9.69% and the S&P finished flat; missiles hit at a carrier and crude fell. Waller made September about CPI rather than oil, so a barrel no longer converts into a rate hike. That holds until an escorted convoy is successfully attacked — the one event that would reprice insurance, freight and the inflation path at once.
